stem: A patient sustains a penetrating injury that removes only the smooth covering from the opposing bone ends of a freely movable joint. Which tissue has been directly damaged?

During assessment of a joint, the nurse notes that the articulating bones are united by dense connective tissue and no joint cavity is present. Which functional property is MOST consistent with this structural arrangement?
options: Movement limited primarily by synovial fluid viscosity

stem: A client has degeneration of a structure that normally reduces friction, distributes load, and prevents direct bone-to-bone contact at a synovial articulation. Which structure is primarily affected?
A student states that synovial fluid is secreted by the articular cartilage. Which correction by the instructor is MOST accurate?
options: It is produced by the fibrous capsule and stored in bursae.
It is secreted by the synovial membrane and nourishes avascular articular cartilage.
It is produced by ligaments and absorbed by tendons.
It is secreted by periosteum and lubricates only non-articular surfaces.

stem: A patient with severe inflammation of the inner lining of a knee joint is expected to have impaired production of which substance?
A joint permits flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, rotation and circumduction. Which synovial joint type BEST explains this range?
Which observation BEST distinguishes a pivot joint from a hinge joint?
options: Movement occurs around a longitudinal axis rather than predominantly in one plane.
The joint possesses articular cartilage rather than fibrocartilage.
The joint lacks a capsule but contains synovial fluid.
Movement is possible only when a bursa is present.

stem: A client can flex and extend a joint but cannot normally abduct it. Which joint type is MOST consistent with this finding?
Which movement describes decreasing the angle between two articulating bones?
A nurse asks a patient to move an upper limb away from the body's median plane. Which movement is being tested?
A patient returns the abducted arm toward the trunk. Which movement has occurred?
A clinician asks a patient to trace a large circle with the distal end of an extended upper limb while the proximal end remains relatively fixed. Which movement is demonstrated?
A lesion prevents the head of the humerus from rotating within the glenoid cavity but leaves flexion and extension partly intact. Which movement is MOST directly lost?
A patient has damage to the glenohumeral joint. Which characteristic explains why this joint sacrifices stability for mobility?
options: A deep socket tightly encloses most of the humeral head.
A relatively shallow glenoid cavity articulates with a large humeral head.
The joint is stabilized primarily by an interosseous membrane.
The humerus and scapula are united by fibrocartilage.

stem: Which structure MOST directly deepens the socket of the shoulder without converting it into a fixed articulation?
A patient tears the tendons that blend with and reinforce the capsule around the shoulder. Which stabilizing mechanism is compromised?
A patient can flex the elbow but cannot extend it against resistance. Which muscle is MOST likely impaired?
Which articulation is primarily responsible for the hinge-like flexion and extension of the elbow?
A client experiences pain when rotating the forearm so the palm turns posteriorly in anatomical position. Which movement is being performed?
A fracture compromises the proximal radioulnar articulation. Which movement would be MOST specifically impaired?

A patient with median nerve compression beneath a strong fibrous band at the anterior wrist is diagnosed with carpal tunnel syndrome. Which structure forms the superficial boundary implicated in the compression?
Which structures normally pass through the carpal tunnel with the median nerve?
A patient cannot bring the thumb across the palm to touch a fingertip. Which specialized movement is impaired?
The first carpometacarpal joint permits greater mobility than the corresponding joints of digits 2â5 primarily because it is what type of synovial joint?
A patient has an isolated injury to an interphalangeal joint. Which movement pair should remain characteristic of that joint?
Metacarpophalangeal joints permit flexion, extension, abduction, adduction and circumduction. Which classification BEST fits these joints?
A client with severe hip trauma has disruption of the fibrocartilaginous rim surrounding the acetabulum. What is the MOST likely mechanical consequence?
options: Reduced depth and stability of the acetabular socket

stem: Which feature makes the hip generally more stable than the shoulder despite both being ball-and-socket joints?
options: The hip lacks a joint capsule.
The acetabulum forms a deeper socket around the femoral head.
The hip contains no articular cartilage.
The femoral head is held only by muscle tone.

stem: A patient has damage to the ligament running from the acetabular region to the head of the femur. Which joint is involved?
A nurse evaluates a patient who cannot move the thigh away from the median plane. Which hip movement is deficient?
Which statement BEST describes the knee joint?
options: It is a simple pivot joint with a single articulation.
It is a complex synovial joint involving femur, tibia and patella.
It is a cartilaginous joint stabilized only by fibrocartilage.
It is a ball-and-socket joint whose socket is formed by the tibia.

stem: A patient tears a cruciate ligament. Which normal function is MOST directly compromised?
options: Stabilization of the femur-tibia relationship during knee movement
Attachment of the patella to skin

stem: Which pair of structures consists of fibrocartilaginous pads that improve congruence between femoral and tibial articular surfaces?
A twisting injury causes a tear of a knee meniscus. Which function is MOST likely reduced?
options: Load distribution and stabilization between femur and tibia
Active extension generated by quadriceps contraction
Transmission of impulses through the tibial nerve

stem: The patella is embedded within the tendon of which muscle group?
A patient cannot actively extend the knee after complete disruption of the quadriceps mechanism. Which structure normally transmits quadriceps force from the patella toward the tibia?
Which movement at the knee is produced principally by the quadriceps femoris?
Which muscle group is principally responsible for knee flexion?
A patient has a swollen friction-reducing sac adjacent to a joint. Which structure is inflamed?
What is the primary role of a bursa located where a tendon passes over bone?
options: Increase friction to stabilize the tendon
Prevent all movement of the tendon

stem: A patient cannot raise the toes toward the shin. Which ankle movement is impaired?
A patient is asked to stand on tiptoe. Which movement must occur at the ankle?
Which muscle group is MOST directly associated with dorsiflexion of the ankle?
Which muscles are the principal plantar flexors identified in the chapter?
A patient has an injury between the distal tibia, distal fibula and talus. Which joint is affected?
The medial malleolus is the distal projection of which bone?
The lateral malleolus is formed by the distal end of which bone?
Which bone receives the body weight from the tibia at the ankle articulation?
A patient has disruption of the strong medial ligament complex of the ankle. Which name identifies this structure?
A patient has intact ankle dorsiflexion and plantar flexion but difficulty turning the sole medially. Which movement is impaired?
Turning the sole of the foot laterally is termed which movement?
Most joints between the bones of the ankle and foot are structurally classified as which type?
Long tendons crossing the ankle are enclosed in synovial sheaths primarily to achieve what effect?
A patient has degeneration of articular cartilage but an intact synovial membrane. Why is cartilage repair still limited?
options: Articular cartilage has no direct blood supply.
Synovial fluid completely prevents cell division.
The cartilage is composed only of elastic fibers.
Articular cartilage is outside the joint capsule.

stem: Which age-related change in articular cartilage MOST directly increases stress on underlying bone?
options: It becomes thinner and less compressible.
It becomes thicker and more vascular.
It secretes increasing quantities of synovial fluid.
It transforms into dense regular connective tissue.

stem: A joint is enclosed by a sleeve of fibrous tissue and lined internally by a membrane that secretes lubricating fluid. Which structural class is described?
A child has a temporary joint in which cartilage lies between the epiphysis and diaphysis of a growing long bone. Which structure is being described?
Which example BEST represents a fibrous joint designed for essentially no movement?
A tooth is anchored in its socket by fibrous connective tissue. Which structural joint category does this represent?
A patient has pathology of an intervertebral disc that normally permits limited movement between adjacent vertebral bodies. Which structural joint category is primarily represented?

Case: After a football injury, a patient reports knee instability. Imaging shows intact menisci but disruption of a ligament located within the joint that restrains abnormal displacement between tibia and femur. Which structure is MOST likely injured?

Case: A patient falls on an outstretched hand and later has numbness in the lateral palm and difficulty with thumb opposition. Swelling beneath the flexor retinaculum would MOST directly compress which nerve?
Case: Following shoulder trauma, the humeral head repeatedly slips because the fibrocartilaginous structure that deepens the socket is torn. Which structure is damaged?
Case: A patient with ankle trauma can dorsiflex normally but cannot plantar flex against resistance. Which muscle pair should the nurse suspect FIRST?
Case: A client has pain when the sole is forcibly turned outward after an ankle injury. Which movement provokes the pain?

Case: A patient has loss of smooth, low-friction movement in a synovial joint despite normal muscle strength. The cartilage remains structurally intact, but its nutritional support is impaired. Dysfunction of which structure BEST explains the finding?
Case: A patient has preserved elbow flexion-extension but loses the ability to rotate the radius around the ulna. Which joint mechanism is MOST likely disrupted?
Case: A patient can flex and extend the fingers but cannot spread them apart at the metacarpophalangeal joints. Which movement is selectively impaired?
Case: An older adult has progressive thinning and reduced compressibility of knee articular cartilage. Which consequence should the nurse anticipate MOST directly?
options: Greater transmission of mechanical stress to underlying bone
Increased vascular perfusion of the cartilage
Complete loss of synovial fluid secretion
Conversion of the knee into a fibrous joint

stem: Case: Trauma destroys the capsule of a synovial joint but leaves the articular cartilage intact. Which immediate mechanical function is MOST directly compromised?
options: Enclosure and stabilization of the articulation
